extracted.intended_audience: Ph.D. students applying for NIA (NIA/NIH) F31 predoctoral fellowships in aging research
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting an NIA NRSA Individual Predoctoral F31 fellowship application for Ph.D. students conducting aging research, including eligibility, deadlines, budget caps, and component length limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Citizenship/Residency
rubrics_metrics.description: F31 recipients must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents at the time of award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: Dissertation-stage Ph.D. students
rubrics_metrics.description: Ph.D. students who are at the dissertation stage by time of award (research lab chosen).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should have a research lab chosen and be at the dissertation stage by the award start date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of research topic for NIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline: All aging research. Applicants should ensure their research topic fits NIA's scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the list of currently funded NIA F31s to see examples; to request feedback on topic appropriateness, submit a one-page overview of specific aims to NIATraining@mail.nih.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deadlines and receipt cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: Yearly Due Dates: April 8, August 8, December 8 with three NIH NRSA fellowship cycles per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receipt cycles map to review and earliest award start dates (e.g., April 8 receipt → June/July initial review → December earliest award start). Applicants must meet the listed receipt dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum award duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum Award Duration: Five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graduate students may receive up to 5 years of combined support from the F31 award and any institutional T32 program; confirm with your graduate program director if you have prior T32 funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipend and funding components (2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: Yearly award budgets are composed of stipends, tuition and fees, and institutional allowance. (2025 amounts listed.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 2025 amounts: Stipend $28,788; Maximum Tuition $16,000; Institutional Allowance $4,750. Updated levels are described in NOT-OD-25-105.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tuition payment cap rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Tuition and fees paid can be 60% of total institutional tuition, or $16,000, whichever is less.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional allowance permitted uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional Allowance may be used to cover expenses such as health insurance, research supplies, equipment, books, and travel to scientific meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Childcare costs allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each fellow may request $3,000 per year to defray childcare costs from a licensed provider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the FAQs on Childcare Costs for details and eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting a study section / assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: To choose a study section to indicate on your Assignment Request Form, consult the list of NIH Fellowship study sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should identify an appropriate NIH fellowship study section when completing the Assignment Request Form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract component must be no more than 30 lines of text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere strictly to the 30-line limit when preparing the application abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Narrative must be 3 sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the Project Narrative concise and limited to three sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate Biosketch length and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidate Biosketch: 5 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A biosketch is a document containing a curriculum vitae (CV), personal statement, and description of past research experience; follow SF424 (R&R) and NIH biosketch formats and instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor Biosketch length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor Biosketch: 5 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a sponsor biosketch following NIH format and the 5-page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate Goals, Preparedness, and Potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidate Goals, Preparedness, and Potential section: 3 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe career goals, evidence of preparedness and potential for a research career within the 3-page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Activities and Timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Training Activities and Timelines section: 3 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear training plan and timeline fitting within the 3-page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Training Project Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Training Project Specific Aims: 1 page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List concise, well-scoped specific aims on a single page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Training Project Strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Training Project Strategy: 6 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the training-relevant research strategy in up to 6 pages (methods, rationale, etc.), following SF424 (R&R) guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor(s) Commitment section
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor(s) Commitment: 6 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors should document their commitment to the candidate and training in up to 6 pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support from Collaborators, Contributors, and Consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of Support from Collaborators, Contributors, and Consultants: 6 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include appropriate letters documenting collaboration and resource commitments, abiding by the 6-page combined limit as indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letters requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: 3-5 Reference Letters, 2 pages each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain 3 to 5 reference letters, each no longer than 2 pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find detailed application instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed instructions for each application part can be found in the SF424 (R&R) Application Guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the SF424 (R&R) Application Guide for formatting, component assembly, and technical submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised fellowship application and review process (effective Jan 25, 2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective for receipt dates on or after January 25, 2025, fellowship review criteria have been revised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must read and apply the changes described in NOT-OD-24-107: Implementation of Revisions to the NIH and AHRQ Fellowship Application and Review Process; review the linked guidance on changes to fellowship review criteria and applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of sample F31 applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample F31 applications are available from the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sample applications as examples of formatting and content, while ensuring compliance with NIA-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact for questions and pre-submission feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions about the F31 award for aging or dementia research can be directed to Jamie Lahvic, Ph.D., at NIATraining@mail.nih.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To request feedback on appropriateness of topic, submit a one-page overview of specific aims; a scientific program official will follow up.
